title: Relative identity-component inclusion
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $B,N$ group schemes over $S$ (group objects, with homomorphisms preserving the multiplication and unit [def-sc-group-scheme]), and $j:B\to N$ an $S$-morphism. Define $\operatorname{IsRelativeIdentityComponent}(j)$ to mean that $j$ is a group homomorphism and an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and morphism $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the image of the base-changed morphism $j_s:B_s\to N_s$ [def-pc-base-change] is exactly the connected component of the identity point of $N_s$ [def-weil-connected-scheme]. The identity point is the image of the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ under the unit section. Thus the source has the full open-subscheme structure of the fibrewise identity component, not a reduced induced structure.

source.place: BLR §10.1, Definition 1 and Proposition 9, pp.289 and 294–295; primary scan https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf
